issues.legal_issue: A party cannot challenge on appeal a finding that the property was not joint family property after allowing that finding to become final by failing to appeal or object to it.
A minor is legally capable of receiving ownership of immovable property as a transferee.
The registered sale deeds transferred ownership of the property to the purchaser, and the asserted benami arrangement did not invalidate those transfers.
Once a plaintiff establishes title, the defendant bears the burden of proving acquisition of title by adverse possession for the statutory period.
Permissive possession as a lessee cannot become adverse possession without proof of an open, continuous, hostile possession and the date it became adverse to the true owner's title.
Under Article 65 of the Limitation Act, limitation begins when the defendant's possession becomes adverse, not when the plaintiff acquires ownership.
Concurrent findings may be set aside where they are perverse, including where they disregard relevant evidence or rest on no evidence.
